newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda says Mobutu's downfall is matter for Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda says Mobutu's downfall is matter for Zaire.

text.p: Rwanda's government said on Friday the stepping down from power by Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko was a matter for Zaire alone.
"This isn't really our concern," said Joseph Bideri, the Rwandan government spokesman. "It is a Zairean business as far as we are concerned."
Rwanda has openly backed Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, the rebel force that in October began the offensive that has brought about Mobutu's fall.
But Kigali has constantly denied providing arms or soldiers to the rebel cause despite large numbers of troops in eastern Zaire speaking Kinyarwanda, the Rwandese language.
"We are watching the situation, but our chief concern is that there should be no bloodshed for Kinshasha," Bideri said.

Told that a government statement from Kinshasha said Mobutu would retain his title but give up power, and that there were reports Mobutu would go into exile, Bideri said: "It is difficult to see how you can be called president when you are not -- particularly if you are in a different country."
Kabila's forces drew early strength from ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge tribesman who settled in eastern Zaire from Rwanda about 200 years ago.
While capturing eastern Zaire, the rebels also attacked refugee camps that were home to thousands of Hutu extremists who were launching raids on Rwanda.
